text.title: Freelancer Payment Chase Script Library Output Contract
text.summary: Draft-07 JSON Schema for the chase ladder of one invoice: the six invoice facts pinned to the source of record, the contractual or statutory basis for any fee, exactly three rungs clocked at T+3 / T+10 / T+30 from the due date with per-rung constraints, the stop state, the send log and the terms change at renewal. Validator: `scripts/validate-freelancer-payment-chase-script-library.py`.

section.title: JSON Schema (draft-07)
section.note: What the schema cannot express and the reviewer checks by hand: each `scheduled_date` equals `invoice.due_date` plus `offset_days` (r-three-rungs-clocked-from-due-date); the polite rung's recipients equal the recipient of the invoice and the firm rung adds `parties.client.finance_contact` (r-polite-rung-assumes-oversight, r-firm-rung-deadline-and-named-consequence); `consequence_reference` and `ledger_total_with_interest` derive from `contract.late_payment_basis` and nothing else (r-fees-and-leverage-only-from-contract-or-statute); a `legal` entry in `send_log` is preceded by a `polite` and a `firm` entry (r-legal-rung-is-formal-letter-before-action); `send_log` gains no entry after `status.halted` (r-stop-on-payment-dispute-or-exhaustion); `renewal_terms_change` is set from `days_to_pay` at renewal (r-log-every-send-and-response).

example.note: Subject violations: only two rungs (r-three-rungs-clocked-from-due-date); the polite rung is clocked at T+1, mentions a fee and legal action, runs to 240 words and asks no payment-date question (r-polite-rung-assumes-oversight); the firm rung goes to the sponsor only with a pay-by date 25 days out and a "5% weekly late fee" that no clause or statute grants (r-firm-rung-deadline-and-named-consequence, r-fees-and-leverage-only-from-contract-or-statute); and the status says paid in full while the ladder is not halted and the balance is still 4800 (r-stop-on-payment-dispute-or-exhaustion).

antipattern.description: A `scheduled_date` that is not `invoice.due_date + offset_days`, an `offset_days` other than 3 / 10 / 30, or fewer than three rungs.
antipattern.reason: r-three-rungs-clocked-from-due-date: a rung ahead of its clock reads as a complaint about an invoice that was barely late.

antipattern.description: `consequence_reference` or `ledger_total_with_interest` present while `contract.late_payment_basis.kind` is `none`, or a rate that does not appear in `late_payment_basis.rate`.
antipattern.reason: r-fees-and-leverage-only-from-contract-or-statute: an unenforceable fee hands the client a reason to dispute the whole invoice.

antipattern.description: The polite rung with `mentions_fee_or_consequence` or `mentions_legal_action` true, `word_count` above 120, or `asks_confirmed_payment_date` false.
antipattern.reason: r-polite-rung-assumes-oversight: the message that gets paid fastest is the one finance can forward without answering.

antipattern.description: The firm rung with a single recipient, or without `parties.client.finance_contact` among its recipients.
antipattern.reason: r-firm-rung-deadline-and-named-consequence: the sponsor has no authority over payments.

antipattern.description: `send_log` gains an entry after `status.halted` is true; `payment_status` is `paid_in_full` or `dispute_raised` is true while `halted` is false; `partial` payment without a recomputed `outstanding_balance`.
antipattern.reason: r-stop-on-payment-dispute-or-exhaustion: a chase the morning after payment landed is the most damaging message in the library.

antipattern.description: A rung sent with no `send_log` entry, a log entry without `response`, or `renewal_terms_change` left at `none` when `days_to_pay` exceeds the net terms.
antipattern.reason: r-log-every-send-and-response: without the log the client's payment history is never turned into terms.

text.reference: Stdlib-only validator for this contract; `--self-test` runs both examples above.
Ladder skeleton with the same sections and field names.
